subject.title: Feature Request: Image batching / media group buffering at gateway layer

question: Should channels without native grouping metadata, starting with LINE, support opt-in same-sender media batching, or should OpenClaw keep only native/explicit grouping such as Telegram media_group_id?
rationale: The remaining behavior adds delayed webhook semantics and a public config surface for platforms without reliable album ids, so automation should not choose defaults, batching keys, or flush policy.

options.title: Add LINE opt-in batching
options.body: Add a conservative LINE plugin option that batches only same-account, same-conversation, same-sender downloadable media with documented latency and reply-token tradeoffs.

options.title: Design shared contract first
options.body: Define a media-aware channel SDK/core contract before changing LINE, accepting broader architecture and compatibility review.

options.title: Do not support heuristic batching
options.body: Keep native Telegram album buffering only and document that channels without grouping metadata dispatch media events individually.

recommendation.title: Add LINE opt-in batching
recommendation.body: Add a conservative LINE plugin option that batches only same-account, same-conversation, same-sender downloadable media with documented latency and reply-token tradeoffs.

likelyOwner.reason: This is mainly a product/config-boundary decision, and steipete has the strongest cross-channel media/config history in the reviewed evidence.
